acceptance_criteria.description: Every bridge write and completion is deadline-bounded; the sole writer is explicitly owned, poisoned on ambiguity, and demonstrably terminated on all session exits with no buffered lifecycle replay or surviving socket task.
Writer failure is durably and independently observable with no check-then-wait lost-wakeup window, and deterministic race coverage proves an idle serving loop wakes and terminates promptly.

Malformed, oversized, or timed-out authenticated control input preserves one exact non-reconnectable terminal cause even when the deferred critical lane is full; sibling presence EOF cannot become clean shutdown or reconnect evidence.

Writer requests retain class and readiness generation; reboot cutover discards queued old-generation lifecycle frames, and any unsafe in-flight frame retires the bridge before the new generation can be used.

The pre-ready regression synchronizes only after decode, generation stamping, and presence admission, then proves the stale record allocates no outer sequence and never forwards while a fresh post-ready record does.

All four original correction regressions and new blocked-writer, terminal-cause, generation-cutover, teardown, and barrier tests pass on the real serving path without weakening checkpoint or shutdown behavior.
The full sidecar suite, strict Clippy, formatting, and diff checks pass; root observation contains only server.rs and the staged combined dependency tree remains exact.

closed_decisions: Preserve authenticated bounded JSONL control protocol v2 and coop/crates/coop-sidecar/src/control.rs exactly; every production and test change is confined to server.rs.
Treat the staged combined candidate tree da385949706ef78081fbd0e6145b394bd4b70218 as immutable dependency context; leave the index untouched and produce only one unstaged server.rs correction delta.

Make the sole bridge writer an explicitly owned session resource. Bound every socket write and completion wait by the existing bridge-frame deadline, poison and close the connection after timeout or partial failure, and join or abort-and-await the writer on every completion, overflow, reconnect, reset, shutdown, and error exit.
Publish bridge-writer failure through durable stateful terminal signaling with register-then-recheck semantics; notification delivery may not depend on an unstored Notify permit.

Publish one independently wakeable authoritative control-reader terminal cause shared by critical and presence lanes. Presence-channel closure alone may never authorize reconnect, retained state, clean shutdown, or replacement control before the exact decoder terminal is observed.

Carry request class and readiness generation through writer admission. A confirmed reboot performs an ordered cutover that discards queued old-generation lifecycle work before SESSION_READY; any in-flight lifecycle write that cannot be fenced poisons and retires the bridge instead of crossing generations.

Move the pre-ready regression barrier to a server-owned point after full decode, generation stamping, and bounded presence admission; prove stale work consumes no bridge sequence and is not replayed after authentication.

Preserve the prior fixes for initial active ROM_READY, independently wakeable PresenceQueueFull, readiness-generation stamping, sequence allocation, critical shutdown reservation, and stable redacted failures.
Do not reconnect, remint, retry lifecycle records, or restart realtime after reset, lifecycle-terminal, writer failure, overflow, or control ambiguity in one authenticated session.
forbidden_changes: Do not edit control.rs, launcher, protocol, realtime-core, cloud, server-service, ROM, Lua, Cargo, documentation, generated artifacts, or orchestration files.
Do not weaken authentication, the 512-byte LF-inclusive JSONL bound, epoch or sequence validation, checkpoint semantics, shutdown reservation, error redaction, or reconnect cleanup.
Do not add credentials, endpoint data, generic serde_json::Value, arbitrary bytes, unbounded queues, silent lifecycle loss, cancellable partial-frame reuse, a second bridge writer, or detached tasks.
Do not stage, commit, branch, fetch, pull, push, contact remotes, create or remove worktrees, or revert another worker's edits; preserve the sealed index and all unowned content.
objective: Repair the exact rejected sidecar control-v2 candidate so bridge-writer ownership, terminal-cause delivery, generation cutover, and readiness proofs are bounded and fail-closed without changing the public control contract.

return_when: Every acceptance criterion is resolved and every required command outcome is recorded.
A safe correction requires changing the frozen public or cross-unit boundary.
A concrete toolchain failure prevents further progress within the execution budget.
